title: 3.2 Stage 1: Graph-based Script Planning
use_cases: Use when deriving thematic titles from a baseline premise using a Title Generator.
Implement when constructing structured event graphs with causal, foreshadowing, or suspense attributes.
Configure when modeling character sociodynamics including persona slots and typed relationship categories.
Use when aligning character goals and conflicts with a narrative's causal event skeleton.
content:
First, a Title Generator 𝒩\mathcal{N} derives a thematic title from the premise PP (see Prompt LABEL:prompt:title in Appendix). Subsequently, a Joint Graph Generator 𝒢\mathcal{G} constructs the initial event and character graph representation, explicitly delineating both causal event dependencies and the web of character relationships (see Prompt LABEL:prompt:story_graph in Appendix):

| G(0)=𝒢​(𝒩​(P),P)\qquad G^{(0)}=\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{N}(P),P) | (1) |
| --- | --- |

where G(0)=(Ge(0),Gc(0))G^{(0)}=(G_{e}^{(0)},G_{c}^{(0)}) denotes the initial joint graph structure.

##### Event Graph Construction.

Following Causal Network Theory Trabasso and van den Broek (1985), the Event Graph Ge=(Ve,Ee)G_{e}=(V_{e},E_{e}) functions as the causal skeleton. Each node ve∈Vev_{e}\in V_{e} represents a distinct plot event with explicit attributes, including event ID, event description, narrative stage (e.g., Rising Action, Climax), and time index. The directed edges EeE_{e} are not merely temporal links but encode narrative relation labels ρ​(e)∈{Causal,Foreshadowing,Suspense}\rho(e)\in\{\textsc{Causal},\textsc{Foreshadowing},\textsc{Suspense}\}. The Event Graph is generated through a structured prompt that instantiates these node attributes and edge relations under the above constraints (see Prompt LABEL:prompt:story_graph in Appendix).

##### Character Graph Construction.

The Character Graph Gc=(Vc,Ec)G_{c}=(V_{c},E_{c}) captures the sociodynamics of the narrative world. Each node vcv_{c} encodes multi-dimensional persona slots—including core personality trait, internal conflict, external goal, and hidden secret—while edges EcE_{c} represent evolving relationships with typed categories (Conflict, Cooperative, Emotional, Hidden) Spilka (1973). The Character Graph is generated simultaneously with the Event Graph using Prompt LABEL:prompt:story_graph in the Appendix, ensuring alignment between character relationships and plot events.
